overall: The registered H1 results are accurately reported: five of 32 arms have p<0.05 (one large negative, one smaller negative, three positives of about 0.06), and the report flags the lack of multiplicity correction. The positive effects are small, their intervals nearly reach zero, and they would not survive any correction. Several arms have only about 120 respondents. The main caveat is that the five hits are few relative to 32 uncorrected tests. The E1 prose also contradicts its own table, because completers-only estimates are identical to the originals, so that check shows no real robustness.

issues.issue: The text reports '7.5% of the sample dropped' and 'standard errors unchanged (ratio 1.00)'. The E1 table shows compl_n = 7803 = orig_n in every visible row, so no respondents were dropped in the model sample, and the 7.5% figure appears in no table.
issues.fix: Remove the 7.5% figure, or state that the completers model used the same 7,803 rows as the original model.
issues.disposition_reason: The 7.5% figure is not in the tables and the completers sample equals the original, so the text needs correcting.

issues.issue: The text says 'five of 32 arm-by-gender interactions' are significant. Only 12 rows are visible, and 2 of them have p<0.05 (A4 0.022, A11 0.028). The count of five is not verifiable from the shown table.
issues.fix: Report the count only if it is confirmed by the full table (20 more rows).
issues.disposition_reason: The full-table summary confirms 5 of 32, so the count stands and only the wording needs clarifying.

issues.issue: The text says 'two of 32' arms are significant and the average estimate is 0.004. Only A12 (p=0.048) is visible as significant, and the average of the 32 estimates is not in any table.
issues.fix: Confirm against the full table or remove the count and mean.
issues.disposition_reason: The summary line confirms 2 of 32 significant; only the untabulated mean needs to be sourced or removed.

issues.issue: The text says the three positive videos have 'about 0.06' effects and that the intervals 'approach zero'. The Video 12 CI is [0.005, 0.123], and the prose writes it as 0.005 to 0.12 while the other CIs are given to 2 decimals. The p-values are also given as p=0.012 and p=0.034 in the text, which is consistent. The Video 15 CI is reported as [0.01, 0.11] against the table's [0.014, 0.112], a rounding difference only.
issues.fix: Use table precision: Video 15 CI [0.014, 0.112]; Video 12 CI [0.005, 0.123].
issues.disposition_reason: This is a rounding mismatch in the confidence intervals; use table precision.

issues.issue: Overstated claim: "The other 27 arms were not distinguishable from control.". All 27 have p>0.05, but the CIs are wide (e.g. A4 [-0.187,0.031]), so this shows no detected difference rather than no effect.
issues.fix: Say 'no difference detected' for the other 27 arms.
issues.disposition_reason: claim checked against the tables by the checking agent

issues.issue: Overstated claim: "Restricting to finishers (7.5% dropped) leaves 5 of 32 significant; standard errors unchanged". E1 table: compl_n = orig_n = 7803 and estimates are identical in every row, so no respondents were dropped from the model sample; the 7.5% appears in no table.
issues.fix: State that the completers model used the same 7,803 rows, so the check is uninformative, and drop the 7.5% figure.
issues.disposition_reason: claim checked against the tables by the checking agent
